trickyParts: The rig that proves this change is still standing on the issue's volume and the tester can reuse it rather than rebuild it: /legion/scratch/pgharness (Postgres 17 + pgvector unpacked from Debian packages, started by `bash /legion/scratch/pgharness/start.sh`, which is idempotent; it serves 127.0.0.1:5433 as DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/postgres?sslmode=disable, which every Postgres-backed Go test here needs), and /legion/scratch/tmp/rig (the scratch Go module whose `render` and `render-denied` call Envoy's own production renderer, `sub` subscribes as a session, `render-frame.ts` drives renderInbound, plus the built envoy-dispatch and the captured frames under frames2/). Two nats-servers are running on 127.0.0.1:4333 (granted) and :4334 (notifications.> withheld). Nothing of it is in the workspace or the commit.

events.Quiet is asked of two payload shapes: the typed value at append time (Broker.Notify) and the map[string]any the outbox scanned out of Postgres at publish time. Any arm of it that reads a typed payload is silently false in the outbox - which is the defect this round's last commit fixes for a targeted message and a quiet ask edit. A future arm must read both shapes, as targetedMessage, quietAskEdit and namedVersion do.

The denial a JetStream publish gets is read off the connection's last error, because the server acknowledges a refused publish with nothing. That inherits confirmPublished's documented ambiguity: nats.go keeps one last error per connection, so a violation of another subject recorded in between leaves this publish named unavailable instead.

packages/envoy/infra is a Go module of its own; `go vet`/`go test` there rewrite its go.work.sum as a toolchain side effect. Restore it (jj restore packages/envoy/infra/go.work.sum) before committing, or the commit carries pruned sums nothing asked for.
deviations: The plan put `quiet` on DispatchEventBase in packages/contracts. It is declared as PublishedDispatchEvent (DispatchEvent & { quiet?: boolean }) instead, beside DispatchEventSchema, because the field exists only on the copy the outbox publishes to NATS (outbox/publisher.go envelope), never on the API's event shape, and DispatchEventBase is pinned key-for-key by src/live.test.ts against fixtures/live/event.json: declaring it there forced an Exclude<> exception into that pin for a field the API never sends. DispatchEventSchema is unchanged, and needs no change: renderInbound reads quiet off the raw wire value, not off the parsed data, and a z.object strips unknown keys.

The plan's implementer proof ran task 4's live test and fed its envelope to renderInbound. That lane cannot run in a Legion issue pod at all (it starts NATS through testcontainers, and the pod has no container runtime). Nothing of it is in the workspace, and the next role saves the half-hour of rebuilding it: docs/solutions/legion/a-port-held-in-an-issue-pod-is-a-sibling-roles-harness-move-your-run-with-the-five-port-variables-and-your-own-database-and-never-stop-the-holder-LEGION-695.md is the precedent, and trickyParts above records every path and port.
discoveredComplexity: The adopted #2490 carried a defect its own tests could not see: events.Quiet's typed assertions are false for every event the outbox publishes, so a targeted message and a quiet ask edit went out quiet:false and would have been shown to every session following the issue. The simplify pass's reviewers found it; it is fixed and pinned on the wire in 59c038e. Its tests passed because they called Quiet with typed payloads only.

The counter this issue asked for was silent in the one case it exists for until the same pass found it: a destination whose publish fails before it is recorded (NATS unreachable) returns from publishDestination without reaching attempt.answer, where the counting lives.

packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api cannot run in this pod at all (it refuses a Postgres whose only collation is byte order, which is what an issue pod's initdb --locale=C gives); the suites this change needs - events, outbox, cmd/dispatch, bus - all run here.
openQuestions: D2 is decided, not open: the architect placed the alert in dispatch://INFRA-749 (theorem-labs/agent-infra, blocked by this issue), on the ERROR line rather than on a scrape, since nothing scrapes Dispatch. The line that issue builds on is `dispatch outbox: publish event` at ERROR, whose error names the route, the subject and the server's violation; the pull request body states it as the contract.

D3 (the plan's): criterion 4 cannot pass on a server deploy alone. The client half ships in @sjawhar/pi-envoy and @sjawhar/claude-envoy through the worker image, whose pin lives in the deployment repository, and Legion's production wake never fires on a worker-image pin. The production check reports pending until both halves are live, naming the plugin version it read.
D5 is decided and done, not open: the architect ruled on 2026-10-29 that the synchronous publishJetStream path is fixed in this pull request. It is, in 7112831, with the real-server test above.
